name: Grey celadon
lede: Grey celadon is a soft, muted green that takes its name from celadon ware, the pale jade-green glazed pottery of East Asia, and that our library carries as a rendering of the traditional Japanese Seiji-iro.

sections.title: A pottery green
sections.body:
Our color library lists Grey celadon's source as the traditional Japanese name Seiji-iro (青磁色), glossed there as "celadon color" [1]. *Seiji* is the Japanese word for celadon ware itself, so the name describes the pottery glaze directly rather than a plant or landscape [1]. Celadon glazes, fired across China, Korea and Japan for centuries, range from pale jade to a deeper grey-green; this name sits toward the greyer end [2].

The nearest named color is [[surrey-green|Surrey Green]], 4.1 units away and greener; [[morning-blue|Morning Blue]] sits at 4.3, also greener [2]. In Munsell terms it sits near 3.8G 6.1/2.2: a pale, low-chroma green [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Grey celadon appears in 296 of our 23,781 paintings, as photographed, more common than 68 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 32 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.7 times the expected rate, and Gustav Klimt is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 5 of his 50 works here, 6.7 times his museums' baseline [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color [3]. The earliest match, dated 1470, sits within the archive's documented range for this name, with no earlier record to compare it against here, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
